First, I reported a bug that ended my single player game. Second, I discovered only one of my characters was leveling up in the single player campaign - that will unbalance the campaign very quickly. It is NOT the way D&D plays in any iteration of any D&D game. IF they ever fix single player campaigns, maybe I'll revisit trying this. I like the look and combat of the game but encountering a game ending bug and not being able to level my entire single player team means it's not currently playable as a single player. I am thankful I discovered these before 3 hours passed.

Was so excited to play this as Demeo was a great starting point to then make a full DnD VR game, and honestly I am so utterly disappointed by the lack of effort put into it in the end. This isn't a DnD game, it's a slightly upgraded Demeo with some DnD names slapped on it. Firstly, they won't let you level up or customize your 3 companions in single player, so you'll end up with one levelled main character and 3 lv 1 worthless companions, which is a horrendous design choice, which their lead dev says was made because the game is intended to be played multiplayer. Ok, don't like that, but fine I wanted to play this in VR since it was announced, so finding strangers to join it is. Then you play multiplayer and you have no idea what your team are doing on their turns unless you separately stream your game so you can see, which is again horrendous design and borderline unplayable in VR mode and suggests that multiplayer and teamwork isn't the main thought of the game, and something I honestly don't want to be doing with some random I've never met before. Then throw in some early game bugs, and a massive lack of customisation, the fact you can't change race, class or gender and honestly it makes this simply Demeo with a few DnD keywords plastered over the top.
Challenging game! Would be much better if I can save the game and retry from there.

Got this game to play with friends. In the beginning, it wasn't bad. Decent turn-based action. Plot's not great but not terrible either. Pretty average. Graphics are pretty nice. Audio is pretty well done, although be sure to turn all audio down immediately or be blasted by everything being far too loud. Mine settled at 10% for everything and it's all easy to hear and perfectly understandable. All that said, eventually, after playing for a while, you go through all of the voice lines your characters say every time before they attack or activate an ability. The first couple times, great. After the 50 and 100th time, just shut up and cast your spell, swing your sword, whatever. Just stop wasting my time. The absolutely unforgivable aspect of the game is the random number generator. I get that random numbers are just that. But over the course of several play sessions and two scenarios, we collectively had zero, let me repeat, zero, successful skill rolls for any stat-based rolls of consequence. Find the hidden thing inside the cabin with an easy roll? Nope, fail. Oh, there's a trap! What is it? Poison! Dodge it - Average chance? Nope, fail. You think someone's lying to you? Easy roll to figure out what's actually going on... Nope, fail. Overall, an easy fifteen to twenty skill rolls. All failed. Easy, normal, hard? Doesn't matter. Combat's much the same. Attack? Critical miss. Attack? Critical miss. Attack? Hit for normal damage. Attack a rat with 3 hp that would die from a regular hit? Critical success. How about a damaging taunt where it gives you a chance to hit nearby enemies? No, instead you can have one that can hit nearby enemies or allies! Taunting the enemy hits your adjacent friend! Great! Not only that, but hey.. You're an 'ally' so your taunt can also hit yourself! Great! I can't count the number of times I tried to attack an enemy and instead buffed them. Not an exaggeration, I think hitting enemies with the bard's default attack and critically failing and buffing them instead was about 50/50. At least introduce a 'you missed' combat roll option instead of a 'you missed so hard you made the enemy stronger' or a 'you missed so hard that you wrecked your party member' roll result. Bad luck is one thing. A punishing RNG that seems to have no purpose other than to screw the player out of parts of the story or just to make things more difficult? That's pretty unforgivable. If you're going to go through the trouble of setting up a D20 for skills, at least have the D20 carry over to battle too. Oh, and don't get me started on encounters where the enemies get to go outside the rules of the game, jumping around the entire map, attacking multiple targets and downing PCs. Because that's entirely fair. And the loot. Aside from weapons you get once or twice an adventure that you can only have one of active at any time, all loot is given in cards. Just finish a big encounter? Open a chest for loot? Here's a card. Oh, is your hand full? No reward for you. If it's on steep sale, maybe buy this just to experience the "random" numbers for yourself. Would not recommend at full price or even a moderate discount.

非常有trpg感的crpg。有和朋友们聚在一起在桌子上跑团的感觉。人物是有底座的模型，场地也是方方正正的一块大模型地图。如果把地图缩放到最接近全景的大小，可以看到地图桌子之外是一间干净整洁的温馨房屋，墙上挂满了装饰画。掷骰时骰子也会随着重力滚落到地图上，就像现实中那样。 游戏还是最近更新上的中文，准备之后和朋友一起联机玩。游戏有单人和多人模式，进公众房间通常都能看到有几个房间，还是很热闹的。游戏目前有《混沌余烬》和《冰霜之冠》这两个战役篇章和5个单次地下城冒险。单次地下城冒险更短一些，就是战役篇章中的地图。可以通过在战役篇章中通关来解锁。存档非常灵活，支持多开，可以按条件筛选自己所有的存档。存档相当即时，每次对话和战斗中的行动都会存档。 虽然游戏以战斗为主，每到一个新地方通常就是开战。但并不全是战斗，游戏的主线剧情也很有意思，细节之处不乏有趣的小设计。酒馆里我点了杯猎奇的酒，结果重力翻转把我整个小队都放倒了。任务相关的NPC都有配音。支线任务数量刚刚好，不会多到需要滚轮翻动任务卷轴。在主线任务推进的过程中接取，相对短小，不会占太多的时间。任务地点在地图上有颜色区分。各个地区点击即达，不需要跑图。 战斗系统很有意思，卡牌系统简单易上手。不时能抽到常用的本职技能之外有意思的卡牌，为战斗增加了很多的新意。延迟回合的功能很有用。元素反应的特效也做的很好看。寒冰特效冰锥做的好像真的一样，晶莹透亮。因为是拟真桌游，所以可以直接隔空移动人物。不需要担心人物走路穿过火焰会受伤这样的问题。移动也不会破坏隐匿的状态。不过敌人平移走路可是会受地块影响的哦。 人物死了之后还能小范围内瞎蹦跶，笑死我了。血掉光的角色只要治疗一下就还能拉起来战斗。 就算以死亡状态离开，到下一个地点后，小队全员又会是活蹦乱跳的满血状态。虽然血量不继承，但是手中的卡牌是继承的。手上最多拿10张卡牌，满了的话就拿不了新的奖励卡。即使是在单人游戏中，每个角色的钱袋子也是分开的。所以四人小队，四倍多的钱钱。 [quote] 关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44791929/]游戏好声音[/url]，认真品味好游戏，倾听游戏好声音。 [/quote]

I got into this game after a gigantic Baldur's Gate 3 playthrough and wasn't sure what to expect. Well, I am happy to say that, even though the game is very different from BG3, the experience has been not only refreshing, but surprisingly substantial. As many reviewers pointed out, when it comes to narrative aspect of the game, there are only two campaigns as of now now ( hints in the story pointing toward more coming) consisting of battle areas connected by light threads of a story but this description can easily make it sound like the story is secondary or forced. Well, it is not. The stories of the two campaigns are really well written, NPC lines are crisp and humor is consistently good and unique. Characters can grow on you quickly and the overall vibe is lovely. Voice acting is great and the score is high quality (the variation on the theme in the final boss combat in the second campaign is beyond epic!). When a new playable character was added recently, an episode introducing him was added to and that episode is a true delight for me because it involves certain big names from a classic dnd novel (and I'm a big fan of dnd novels). When it comes to gameplay, it is useful to have in mind that this is not a tabletop dnd simulator even though the two stories definitely build on, and are a wonderful addition to, the Forgotten Realms lore. Instead, mechanics of this game is its own thing. It relies centrally on cards that fill limited number of slots for each character. They can be gained, used and discarded during and outside of combat and economizing cards in hand is among the main aspects of the tactics. Each card gives a character an ability, similar to dnd features. When it comes to difficulty, I played on the default setting, and was surprised how difficult some of the combats can get. Each combat in an arera generates a slithly different map which secures replayability and can shift difficulty slightly. Some criticisms by other reviewrs like inability to level up any character except the avatar in the single-player mode, were obviously solved in the updates before I started playing, because leveling up of the entire party is now very easy. It is true that there is only a limited number of characters with only esthetic customization at character creation but I guess that is a downside only for those expecting a dnd simulator which, as I said, this game is not. The playable characters really do have a lot of, er, character and their comments in the fight are genuinely entertaining. All in all, this is a very very nice game, with lots of lovely detail, and with an occasional surprising level of challenge.

TOO MANY TERRIBLE DESIGN DECISIONS: This could have been a great game if it weren't for all the bad decisions made. 1.) Character "creation" is nothing more than recolor of the premade cookie cutter toons. Not even male/female choice!?! How is that "creating" anything? 2.) Unending respawn of enemies. You'll hate that if you are a "completionist" type player who wants to go back and open every chest, or clear every room. 3.) Useless chests and money in scenarios. You usually have full decks of cards making chests useless, and you usually are already at the very low cap of gold you are allowed to carry, making BOTH pretty useless. 4.) Inability to save. If you dip out between battles during a "quest" you must do all of it all over again. No going back to where you left off. 5.) The RNG they made is ABSOLUTE C.R.A.P. -- I roll a 'skull' (critical miss) *AT LEAST* once every(!!) single(!!) turn!!!!!!! . . . this could have been a fun little game, but there are just TOO many little things that ruin it for me! SUGGESTIONS: - Make male and female versions of each toon, extra points if 2 or 3 variations of each male or female voice lines. - Allow clearing of "maps", or at least stop spawning enemies behind players from rooms already cleared. - Allow the dropping of cards from your heroes deck to accept quest rewards! Or when opening a chest. - Just change the hero gold to party gold where all heroes can pull from. AND DO NOT LIMIT IT! - Allow players to MANUALLY save between battles just because your FKD UP RNG dice. - FIX YOUR RNG!!!! . . . until they do some of these, save your money. Lest be prepared to be disappointed.

I recommend the game. Release was too broken for long (balance and bugs), but now it's way better. Fun both on VR and desktop. More fun when playing coop. The difficulty doesn't scale with the number of players, nor their level. You must choose the difficulty at the beginning of a campaign or mission, and can't change it during a game. It's a bit weird, because in the end the difficulty of a dungeon is based on: - The number of characters - The level of characters - The difficulty picked (between 1-4) - If enemy respawn is disabled or not - If the setting to throw two dice after a fail is enabled or not It's awkward that all of this has to be considered, and good luck to find the right difficulty for each of your game. Gameplay looks very much like Demeo, with added lore, and campaigns. Gameplay mechanisms are identical, but there's a clear difference in how we the game is played. Battlemarked is more forgiving. Numbers (damage, HP, etc) are all increased up. Demeo was very "puzzle-like", where you had to be extra careful on each turn to what to do, in what order, to stay alive. Battlemarked is way more casual, regardless the difficulty. Also, revives are infinite. It's definitely more relaxed, and might not be appealing to more hardcore gamers. Despite the superior content, the game feels less deep than Demeo. The difficulty settings were updated by the dev recently, but the game is still too easy overall. I can do a one shot dungeon with only 2 characters with difficulty 4/4 and no respawn, when the game is designed for 4-characters parties. That said. Spent 260 hours (70 hours in coop) and counting in the game. It's a bit addictive, polished, great sound design and graphics. Stills feel like "small game" because of the lack of depth. I recommend playing the game with at least a friend to see how you like it. Oh, and it was less expensive than Demeo at the release, which is also great.

This review comes from a huge DnD fan. This game just fails flat on everything it tries to achieve. There is 0 roleplay, the story is ok, but it's just NPCs spouting exposition at you. The game is 99 percent combat, this could be fine if the combat evolved at all. You barely grow stronger, the things you do at level 1 will be the same as max level. This is probably the only game, where i get annoyed when i level up, because all my upgrade choices are either bad, meaningless, or RNG dependent. The only piece of equipment you can have on your characters are the weapons and even they are bad and depend on RNG. The cherry on top is that the game takes every opportunity to cheat and make you feel like a bozo for playing good. This is hard to explain, it's more of thing you notice during play, but the most constant thing is that enemies have effects that are not listed, move and attack beyond their reach, and the worst offenders are the bosses, who completely ignore taunts/blocked paths move and attack however they wish multiple times a turn and summon infinite adds. It's a real shame, because the presentation of the game is great(the art style and ability animations), but there is no reason to play this instead of BG3. Update to the review: Some of the achievements are broken and do not unlock (3 did not unlock for now). Got to love playing the campaign for 10+ hours to not unlock the achievement for beating it, and the only way to attempt to unlock it again is to replay the whole thing.... amazing.

It's a fun game that definitely scratches a certain itch. The card mechanics are a little obtuse at times, and the D&D elements are really more branding than anything, but it's still a fun overall package. The characters cover a good spread of different play styles and they have some very fun personalities which manage to come through pretty effectively even though there's no character dialogue. I don't get the same "amateur writing" feeling from the story and narration that some people do, but a fair bit of the quest text does give some major "AI-assisted" vibes to it. Not trying to levy any accusations, but if you've read any amount of AI-generated text you'll know what I'm talking about. It doesn't change my recommendation of the game as a whole, but it's worth knowing about.
